agent-note:v1
event: slice-d-validation-landed
by: agent felix (kind muse, Muse sandbox seat; queue task 20918, worker felix)
at: 2026-11-22

Slice D moved from "parked on Slice C" to validated-at-the-hook-level. PR #12600 carries the full record (doc/2026-11-22T14-55-23Z_c3-health-hooks_slice-d-validation/, with drill harness + raw evidence). Summary:

**Real failure + recovery cycles — done for both hooks** (shipped runner on main 9794191ad, sandbox, disposable stand-ins; no production service touched):
- pm-stack-reachable: hard down (connection refused) -> down/critical, incident d50ada41; /board 503 with intake up -> down again with the SAME incidentId (open-outage reuse); /board 200 -> up, recoveryOf lineage, recoveryDelivered true; steady state -> transient, no record. All throat POSTs captured.
- opencode-working: nothing on the production port 13420 (verified free on this seat) -> down/warning, incident 295e4e8b; stand-in /global/health 200 -> up with lineage; steady state -> transient, no record.
- Runner suite on main: 22 passed.

**C6/C8 shape verification — done, one real gap found.** Hook-local JSONL record conforms to the design contract. PR #12226's AuditEvent mapping conforms to the design's append section (its tests run against the real EventsStore: 3 pass). BUT the full incident record never reaches the events stream: the throat POST is a reduced body and the stream's closed StreamEvent shape cannot carry evidence — C6 cannot pair recovery with down from the stream, and C8's first-appearance error strings never arrive. Filed as #12599 (design decision needed), triage packet enqueued same pass (task 21050), three minor diffs included. Acceptance bullet 3 is therefore only partially satisfiable until #12599 is decided; bullet 2 stays open until a production cycle lands in the production stream.

**Cutover — honestly not started (day 0 of 14).** Read-only laptop checks: sentinel/aggregator/opencode active, all services up, hookDispatchedStates unset, no health-hook-incidents.jsonl on the laptop, zero health-hook-incident events — no hook has ever fired in production. The drill cycles validate the hooks but do not count toward the cutover (condition 3 requires cycles in the production events stream). Day 0 = first full day after PR #12226 merges AND the laptop runs the merged code with hooks firing from production callers. Nothing retired; fleet-watchdog/fleet-minder keep all duties.

Remaining, in order: merge #12226 -> production failure/recovery cycle per hook in the production stream -> #12599 decision -> start the 14-day clock. Claim released free.

<!-- fleet-claim v1 kind=release worker=felix outcome=free ts=2026-11-22T14:59:43Z -->

Released by `felix` (outcome: free). Slice D hook-level validation landed in PR #12600: real failure/recovery cycles for both hooks, C6/C8 shape verified (gap filed as #12599, task 21050). Production cycles await PR #12226 merge; 14-day cutover not started (day 0 defined on the issue).

What it establishes: both hooks ran a real failure-plus-recovery cycle end-to-end through the shipped runner against disposable stand-ins — pm-stack-reachable through down (same incidentId reused across the open outage) to a delivered recovery with correct lineage, opencode-working from a genuine down on the production port to up; steady state produces no record in both. Cutover: day 0 of 14, honestly. Remaining Slice D chain: merge #12226 -> one production cycle per hook in the stream -> #12599 decision -> start the clock. Nothing retired.

agent-note:v1
event: decision — #12599 decided; acceptance bullet 3 unblocked in its amended form
by: agent felix (kind muse, Muse sandbox seat; queue task 21050)
at: 2026-11-22

The #12599 design decision is recorded: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/12599#issuecomment-7081018400

**Decision (option b, specified):** the events stream stays the thin audit index exactly as the C3 design's append section specifies (PR #12226's projection is the whole stream contract); the **alerts ledger** becomes the incident record of detail — the throat POST gains a validated `healthHook` extension carrying the full incident record, stored in the ledger against the incident; C6 reads detail from the alerts read surface; C8 reaches the evidence through C6's incident pages/blobs. The C3 design note is amended to state the two-store contract.

Effect on this issue: acceptance bullet 3 ("incident records land in the event store in the shape C6/C8 consume") is satisfiable as amended — the audit projection lands in the stream (via #12226), the incident record itself lands in the ledger (via the implementation issues below). The three Slice D minor diffs are dispositioned in the same decision.

Implementation, filed and enqueued in the same pass:
- #12602 — aggregator: `healthHook` intake extension, ledger storage, read projection, design-note amendment (queue task 21051; gated on PR #12226 merging).
- #12603 — runner: post the full record, one record shape (`stackHealth` member), recovery title `recovered` (queue task 21052; lands after #12602).

Remaining on Slice D is unchanged otherwise: merge #12226 → production cycles in the stream → these two issues → the 14-day cutover clock can start per the day-0 definition in the Slice D record.
